title: Hosted API marginal cost breakdown by latency slice (working spreadsheet)
content:
Purpose: quick working spreadsheet + synthesis capturing per-token marginal cost across regions and by latency slice. This is an exploratory piece to surface pricing levers (latency-tiered pricing, regional routing, and model-variant fallbacks) and to produce actionable recommendations for the hosted API pricing and routing playbook.

Notes on framing:
- "Latency slice" = p95 response latency bucket for real-time traffic. We split traffic into: ultra-low (<150ms), low (150–300ms), medium (300–800ms), batch-friendly (>800ms).
- Marginal cost here includes: GPU time per token (including packing inefficiencies), networking (egress), and amortized infra overhead (orchestration, cache storage). Not included: R&D, sales, or marketing.
- This is marginal cost per token for a single generation path (no embeddings / no fine-tuning credits).

Key assumptions (editable cells in spreadsheet):
- GPU pool hourly cost by region: us-west-2 = $8.40/hr (A100-80GB reserved-like blended), eu-west-1 = $9.60/hr, ap-southeast-1 = $11.20/hr.
- Effective tokens served per GPU-hour depends on latency slice/batch sizes. Use microbench numbers below.
- Overhead multiplier for orchestration & autoscaling spikiness: 1.12 (12%).
- Network egress per token: 0.00018 USD/token (global average; regional egress varies +/-20%).

Simple micro-bench table (tokens per GPU-hour estimates; conservative):
Region | Latency slice | Typical batch size | tokens/hr/GPU (effective)
us-west-2 | ultra-low (<150ms) | 1–4 | 120,000
us-west-2 | low (150–300ms) | 8–16 | 350,000
us-west-2 | medium (300–800ms) | 32–64 | 1,000,000
us-west-2 | batch (>800ms) | 128+ | 3,200,000
eu-west-1 | ultra-low | 1–4 | 110,000
eu-west-1 | low | 8–16 | 325,000
eu-west-1 | medium | 32–64 | 930,000
eu-west-1 | batch | 128+ | 3,000,000
ap-southeast-1 | ultra-low | 1–4 | 95,000
ap-southeast-1 | low | 8–16 | 280,000
ap-southeast-1 | medium | 32–64 | 820,000
ap-southeast-1 | batch | 128+ | 2,600,000

Derived marginal GPU cost per token (formula):
- base_gpu_cost_per_token = (gpu_hourly_cost / tokens_per_gpu_hour)
- marginal_gpu_cost_per_token = base_gpu_cost_per_token * overhead_multiplier
- total_cogs_per_token = marginal_gpu_cost_per_token + network_egress_per_token

Sample rows (calculated from above assumptions):
Region,Model family,Latency slice,tokens/hr/GPU,gpu_hourly_cost,base_gpu_cost_per_token,overhead_multiplier,marginal_gpu_cost_per_token,network_egress_per_token,total_cogs_per_token,example_price_per_token_usd,example_margin_pct
us-west-2,redwood-1,ultra-low,120000,8.40,0.00007,1.12,0.0000784,0.00018,0.0002584,0.0007,63%
us-west-2,redwood-2-8b,low,350000,8.40,0.000024,1.12,0.000027,0.00018,0.000207,0.0006,65%
eu-west-1,llama2-13b,medium,930000,9.60,0.00001032,1.12,0.00001156,0.00018,0.00019156,0.0005,62%
ap-southeast-1,redwood-1,batch,2600000,11.20,0.000004307,1.12,0.000004823,0.000216,0.000220823,0.00045,51%

Observations from the quick scan:
- Ultra-low latency traffic is ~3–6x more expensive per token than batch-friendly traffic, driven by lower packing/batching efficiency.
- Regional delta is material: ap-southeast-1 shows ~15–25% higher per-token COGS compared to us-west-2 in same latency slice. This is due to higher GPU cost and slightly worse tokens/hr assumptions.
- Network egress is a non-trivial fixed floor (roughly 60–80% of total_cogs in ultra-low examples above). We should validate if we can further reduce egress per token via compression or client-side truncation rules.

Sensitivity scenarios to run in spreadsheet (recommended tabs):
1) Price floor test: vary gpu_hourly_cost ±30% and network_egress_per_token ±50% to compute worst/best margin.
2) Latency-sla mix: change traffic mix (% of ultra-low / low / medium / batch) and simulate P&L for a 10M token month.
3) Model-variant fallback: assume 15% of requests can be downgraded to a quantized 4-bit variant of same family; calculate token savings and quality impact (linked to eval set).
4) Regional routing: test rerouting 20% of non-critical traffic from ap-southeast-1 to us-west-2 using cross-region priority queue and compute latency penalty vs cost savings.

Open questions / follow-ups (to validate before final recommendations):
- Can infra amortization be measured per model-family instead of global multiplier? I.e., do some models incur more orchestration overhead (LLM size, KV cache sizing)? (ENG-2181)
- Precise egress per token by region and whether CDN compression or edge truncation is feasible without breaking session semantics. (SRE/NETWORK)
- Customer impact: how much of ultra-low traffic is truly latency-sensitive vs. habitually provisioned for low latency? Survey top 30 customers by token usage. (CS)

Draft recommendations (short-list):
1) Introduce a latency-tier surcharge for ultra-low SLA: apply a 2.5–3x effective price multiplier or add a small flat per-request surcharge for p95 <150ms. This preserves price simplicity for bulk customers but recovers cost on the high-cost tail.
2) Region-specific price multipliers: make price per token table regional (visible in Console and RateCard) with a discrete apac surcharge of 10–20% until we can reduce local costs.
3) Default model-variant policy: enable opt-in auto-fallback to quantized model variant for non-sensitive routes and provide a "quality budget" knob in Console.
4) Cache & prefix heuristics: aggressively prioritize prefix caching for chat sessions (2–3x effective token savings on follow-ups).
5) Offer a "low-cost routing" toggle for customers to route non-latency-critical requests to cheaper regions or batch queues (with clear latency/availability docs).

Immediate next steps (owners & milestones):
- Spreadsheet: consolidate assumptions into a canonical sheet with scenario tabs and cell comments (owner: Will Nguyen) — target: 2026-03-07.
- Bench: run microbench tokens/hr by model family and latency bucket across us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1 (owner: Lena Fischer) — target: 2026-03-10.
- CS outreach: spike survey of top 30 customers to classify latency requirements (owner: Omar Haddad) — target: 2026-03-14.
- Product/legal: draft pricing page language and examples for latency-tiered pricing (owner: Sofia Patel) — target: 2026-03-21.

Loose ends to document in final repo:
- Save raw bench data in /s3/cost-analysis/latency-slices/ + attach to Confluence page.
- Add a "quality impact" eval tab linking prompt-level regressions when applying model-variant fallback for three representative use cases (chat assistants, summarization, code gen).

Notes to reviewers: this doc is intentionally spreadsheet-first (lots of editable assumptions). Please review the sample numbers and flag any known infra costs we missed (e.g., per-request cold-start tax, stateful session overhead). I plan to iterate with bench data next week and then produce a final recommendation memo to present to Pricing and GTM.
